cards.explanation: The answer is False. Luke says the people thought the kingdom of God would appear “imminently.” (Luke 19:11) That's not a long way off, friends. That's checking the oven every ten seconds. Jesus was near Jerusalem, so He told them a parable.

The answer is do business with it. The man tells his servants, “Conduct business with this until I return…” (Luke 19:13) so the money is meant to go to work. Nobody gets a mina to just sit on it. Hold on to that line, friends, because it matters when the servants come back.
The answer is that they don't want him ruling over them. The delegation says, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) It's short and it's blunt. Nobody could mistake that message.

The answer is True. When the man returns as king, he summons the servants he gave the money to, to find out what each one earned. It's report time. Think of the moment a boss says, "Let's see the numbers."

The answer is that he was faithful in a very small matter. The master says, “Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter…” (Luke 19:17) One mina is the small matter here. The praise is for being faithful, and that's where the reward comes from.

The answer is authority over ten cities. The master says, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) Think about that jump, friends. This servant started with one mina. Now he's looking at ten cities.

The answer is False. The second servant says, “Master, your mina has made five minas.” (Luke 19:18) That's five, not ten. And the master gives him authority over five cities, so his reward matches his report.

The answer is True. The servant says so himself, bakers. He tells the master, “For I was afraid of you…” (Luke 19:21) He puts the mina in a cloth and names his fear as the reason. Those are his own words, and the master will use them in a moment.

The answer is to put it in the bank to earn interest. The master asks, “Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?” (Luke 19:23) It's the simplest move there is. You hand it over, and it grows while you wait.

The answer is ten. The master says, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.” (Luke 19:24) That's the first servant, the one whose mina produced ten more. Those standing by say he already has ten. (Luke 19:25)

The answer is that even what he has will be taken away. The master says, “…the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Luke 19:26) That's exactly what just happened with the mina in the cloth. It's a hard line, friends, but it's what he says.

The answer is the enemies who didn't want him as king. His subjects hated him and sent a delegation that said, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) The master calls them “…these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them…” (Luke 19:27) I think this is a heavy part of the parable, and it's worth slowing down for.
